newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden firm offers free calls with ad breaks.
newsitem.headline: Sweden firm offers free calls with ad breaks.

text.p: A Swedish telephone advertising company is offering free calls to customers willing to put up with their conversations being interrupted by commercial breaks.
The Stockholm-based Gratistelefon, or Free Telephone, has tested its free calls in the Swedish towns of Lund and Norrkoping since November 1 and is now generating about 30,000 calls a day.
Founder Carl Ander said Gratistelefon hopes to make the scheme nationwide by the end of this year and is in negotiations to sell the idea with companies in several other countries.
"We are expanding rapidly," Ander told Reuters. "It is a new media and a lot of companies want to try it."
Callers can get access to the free calls by first calling Gratistelfon's toll-free number and then dialling the number of the person they want to contact.
The trials so far have allowed unlimited calls to anywhere in Sweden.
Adverts are played while the call is connected and then for 10 seconds after the first minute. The 10-second ad breaks then override the call every three minutes.
"As the adverts are only every three minutes it is not really an interruption," Ander said.
Gratistelefon has negotiated discount minutes with Sweden's Tele2, the rival operator to the national operator.
It charges advertisers 0.45 crowns for each contact or person with each 10 second break counting as two contacts.
"Compared to direct marketing it is cheaper but it works out a bit more expensive than radio advertising," said Ander, who set up Gratistelefon about 16 months ago.
"We are focusing more on the fact that we want to be a direct marketing media because we know who is calling and we can choose the right spot."
Ander said Gratistelefon also planned to make the service interactive this year with, for example, callers able to push one to receive a brochure or more information about the advertiser's product.
